project.name: Referral to first session (worked example)
project.researchQuestion: Why do people wait about two weeks for a first support session, and what small change would shorten the wait without more work for the support team?
project.scopeDescription: From a referral that arrives (by the online form or as an email from a partner agency) to the person’s first support session. Partner agencies and peer mentors are outside the reviewed scope, but hand work in and out of it.
project.intendedOutcome: Current-state map, prioritized opportunity sheet and a leadership brief.
project.externalInterfaces: People referred (service users); partner agencies (GP surgeries, housing officers); peer mentors (volunteers).

branches.name: Daily huddle for straightforward cases
branches.hypothesis: A short daily huddle for straightforward cases shortens the wait for a first session and adds little work.

branches.name: Draft from notes, 5 Nov
branches.hypothesis: 2 changes proposed from 17 notes in the archive.

notes.text: Screening is quick when the form is complete. It is the chasing that eats the morning.
notes.rawText: Screening is quick when the form is complete. It is the chasing that eats the morning.

notes.text: Most people don't pick up a withheld number, so I try three or four times over two days.
notes.rawText: Most people don't pick up a withheld number, so I try three or four times over two days.

notes.text: Everything goes into the case system and then again into the spreadsheet, because the meeting only looks at the spreadsheet.
notes.rawText: Everything goes into the case system and then again into the spreadsheet, because the meeting only looks at the spreadsheet.

notes.text: On duty days I also cover the phone line, so screening gets interrupted all the time.
notes.rawText: On duty days I also cover the phone line, so screening gets interrupted all the time.

notes.text: Partner referrals often come without a phone number or consent, and nothing can move until we have them.
notes.rawText: Partner referrals often come without a phone number or consent, and nothing can move until we have them.

notes.text: We allocate every case at the Tuesday meeting so the whole team shares the judgement about risk.
notes.rawText: We allocate every case at the Tuesday meeting so the whole team shares the judgement about risk.

notes.text: A case that finishes intake on a Wednesday waits almost a week for the next meeting.
notes.rawText: A case that finishes intake on a Wednesday waits almost a week for the next meeting.

notes.text: Straightforward cases could be allocated the same day without the full meeting.
notes.rawText: Straightforward cases could be allocated the same day without the full meeting.

notes.text: The spreadsheet is the real waiting list. The case system is for the funder's reports.
notes.rawText: The spreadsheet is the real waiting list. The case system is for the funder's reports.

notes.text: Workers usually see a new case on their list the day after the meeting.
notes.rawText: Workers usually see a new case on their list the day after the meeting.

notes.text: I didn't answer because it was a private number. I thought it was a sales call.
notes.rawText: I didn't answer because it was a private number. I thought it was a sales call.

notes.text: Once I had a date it was fine. It was not knowing for two weeks that was hard.
notes.rawText: Once I had a date it was fine. It was not knowing for two weeks that was hard.

notes.text: The first phone call was the first time someone actually listened.
notes.rawText: The first phone call was the first time someone actually listened.

notes.text: Mentors text me their availability and I update the spreadsheet on Fridays, so by Tuesday it can be out of date.
notes.rawText: Mentors text me their availability and I update the spreadsheet on Fridays, so by Tuesday it can be out of date.

notes.text: Could mentors update their own availability, or would that put people off volunteering?
notes.rawText: Could mentors update their own availability, or would that put people off volunteering?

notes.text: A text first, saying who was calling, would have helped. I would have picked up.
notes.rawText: A text first, saying who was calling, would have helped. I would have picked up.

notes.text: I wanted to talk to a person, not fill in another form.
notes.rawText: I wanted to talk to a person, not fill in another form.

notes.text: Timed 9 screenings: median 15 minutes, range 9 to 24.
notes.rawText: Timed 9 screenings: median 15 minutes, range 9 to 24.

notes.text: Saw the phone ring six times during one 40-minute screening session.
notes.rawText: Saw the phone ring six times during one 40-minute screening session.

notes.rawText: Watched the duty worker retype the intake summary from the case system into the spreadsheet, about 6 minutes per case.

notes.rawText: How many referrals would count as straightforward? Ask the team to sort last month's cases.

insights.title: The weekly meeting sets the pace of allocation
insights.body: A case that finishes intake just after Tuesday waits almost a week, whatever the workload. Seven of the eleven cases at the meeting I watched needed no discussion. Straightforward cases could move faster without losing the shared judgement on complex ones.

insights.title: The spreadsheet is the real waiting list
insights.body: Decisions are made from the spreadsheet, so every case is typed twice: once into the case system for the funder, and once into the spreadsheet for the meeting. Mentor availability is only in the spreadsheet.

insights.title: Phone tag, not screening, delays the first contact
insights.body: Screening takes about 15 minutes. To reach the person takes two or three attempts over two days, because the calls come from a withheld number that people do not answer.

insights.title: The first conversation is what people value
insights.body: People referred describe the first call as the moment that someone listened. A change to intake must keep a conversation with a person.

Could peer mentors hold some first sessions?
Not explored yet. Ask the volunteer coordinator what mentors would want.

links.comment: The procedure says the same day. The case record dates say about a day.
Availability is updated on Fridays, four days before the meeting.
Interruptions can explain part of the wait before screening.
Phone referrals from GP surgeries are not on the map yet.

opportunities.title: Allocate straightforward cases between meetings
opportunities.reportTitle: Allocate straightforward cases the next working day
opportunities.interpretation: The weekly rhythm, not the amount of work, sets the wait for allocation. A short daily huddle could allocate the cases that need no discussion, and the Tuesday meeting could keep the complex ones.
opportunities.uncertainty: The share of straightforward cases comes from one meeting (7 of 11).
opportunities.preserve: Shared judgement about risk at the Tuesday meeting, and the peer support that it gives the team.
opportunities.stakeholders: Duty workers (a daily 10-minute huddle), the team lead (a Friday review of huddle allocations) and people referred (a shorter wait).
opportunities.validationPlan: A six-week trial. Compare the median days from referral to first session and the number of re-allocated cases with September and October.
opportunities.internalNotes: Check the duty rota before we propose a start date.

opportunities.title: Stop typing every case twice
opportunities.reportTitle: Use the case system’s waiting list instead of the spreadsheet
opportunities.interpretation: The case system already has a waiting list view. If the team switches it back on, cases are typed once and there is one record.
opportunities.uncertainty: Nobody has used the view since the update. It may not show mentor availability.
opportunities.preserve: The meeting’s habit of looking at the whole list together.
opportunities.stakeholders: Duty workers (no more retyping), the volunteer coordinator (availability needs a new place) and the team lead.
opportunities.validationPlan: Walk through the view with the team, then run one meeting from it next to the spreadsheet.

opportunities.title: Fewer call attempts before the first conversation
opportunities.reportTitle: Reach people at the first or second call
opportunities.interpretation: People do not answer withheld numbers. A text before the call, or a call-back time chosen on the form, could cut the number of attempts.
opportunities.uncertainty: Whether the phone system can show a number, and what people referred would prefer.

opportunities.title: Replace the intake call with an online form
opportunities.reportTitle: An online intake form instead of the call
opportunities.closeReason: People referred value the first conversation. An online form instead of the call would remove what works.

options.title: Keep the Tuesday meeting for every case
options.benefits: The whole team judges every case. Nobody’s week changes.
options.downsides: Cases that finish intake after Tuesday wait up to six days.

options.title: Daily 10-minute huddle for straightforward cases
options.benefits: Straightforward cases are allocated the next working day: about 1.5 days sooner on average.
options.downsides: Less discussion of cases that look simple but are not.
options.shiftedWork: Duty workers: about 50 minutes a week in huddles. Team lead: a Friday review of the huddle’s allocations.
options.effort: Agree what counts as straightforward. A whiteboard. Two weeks to settle.
options.costs: About 60 GBP for a whiteboard and printed sheets.
options.tradeoffs: A faster start for most people against a little less shared discussion.
options.unknowns: How many cases are straightforward each week. Cover in holiday weeks.
options.test: A six-week trial with the guardrails in the scenario.

options.title: Build an allocation app
options.benefits: It could match cases to workers and mentors automatically.
options.downsides: Months of work. It takes the decision away from the team.
options.unknowns: Whether the case system can export the data that the app needs.

options.title: Switch the case system’s waiting list view back on
options.benefits: Cases are typed once. The record the funder sees is the one the team uses.
options.downsides: The meeting must learn a new screen.
options.shiftedWork: The volunteer coordinator needs a new place for mentor availability.
options.effort: Ask the supplier to switch the view on. One practice meeting.
options.costs: None expected under the current licence.
options.unknowns: Whether the view can show mentor availability.
options.test: Run one meeting from the view next to the spreadsheet.

options.title: Keep the spreadsheet
options.downsides: About 6 minutes of retyping for each case, and two records that can disagree.

options.title: Text before calling, saying who is calling
options.benefits: People know who is calling and can pick up.
options.downsides: Needs a phone that can send texts.
options.test: Two weeks of texts before calls. Count the attempts on the call log.

options.title: Ask for a good time to call on the referral form
options.benefits: Calls come at a time the person chose.
options.downsides: Partner referrals do not use the form.

imports.name: Duty desk shadowing, 1 Oct
imports.text:
Duty desk shadowing
Thu 1 Oct, 09:00 to 12:30, with the duty worker. Names replaced with roles.

- Timed 9 screenings: median 15 minutes, range 9 to 24.
- Saw the phone ring six times during one 40-minute screening session.
- Call log for 14 referrals: 2.5 call attempts on average before reaching the person.
- Watched the duty worker retype the intake summary from the case system into the spreadsheet, about 6 minutes per case.
- Typed-up intakes took about 12 minutes each (4 timed).
- Intake calls I listened to took 25 minutes on average (5 calls).
- Two of the morning's referrals had no phone number, so screening stopped until the details came back.
- A GP receptionist phoned the duty line with a referral, and the duty worker typed it into the online form during the call.

imports.name: Allocation meeting, 6 Oct
imports.text:
Allocation meeting
Tue 6 Oct. Team lead, two duty workers, a support worker and the volunteer coordinator.

The meeting took 90 minutes for 11 cases. Seven of the 11 cases were agreed in under two minutes with no discussion. Three complex cases took most of the time: risk, housing and a safeguarding question.

The lead asked twice whether mentor availability was current. Nobody was sure.

Two of the 11 cases came in by phone from GP surgeries.

imports.name: Referral procedure v3
imports.text:
Referral procedure (version 3, March 2026)

1. Referrals are screened on the day they arrive.
2. Every person referred is contacted within two working days.
3. Allocation takes place at the weekly team meeting.
4. The case record is the single record of each referral.
